notes: TypeSafe Evals tooltips (vendor-run, TypeSafe is the vendor of Jev): Jev vs eight LLM configurations on four workflow tasks, "workflow" vs "prompt" mode. Reference labels are "generated via an average of the responses of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, both at high thinking", so accuracy measures agreement with an LLM consensus; "Structure is always better" is the page claim. Time per case and cost per case are given in tooltips ("model · workflow|prompt · accuracy% · $cost · time s"); the tooltip does not state whether cost and time are per case or per run (the chart axis says "cost per case, USD (log)"). The Luna, Sol and Terra configurations are NOT stored: the page prints no generation (gpt-6 vs gpt-5.6) and Terra has no GPT-6 id in model-catalog. The same four Jev numbers (61.8, 76.0, 61.7, 71.6) are the ones Cloudflare compares Clef against.

claims.statement: TypeSafe Evals: Jev 61.8 / 76.0 / 61.7 / 71.6 accuracy (invoice / customer service / security incidents / agent trace) at $0.0011 / $0.0001 / $0.0001 / $0.0003 per case and 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.3 / 0.5 s, versus Opus 5 in workflow mode 78.4 / 72.4 / 66.2 / 75.2 at $0.4856 / $0.0579 / $0.0574 / $0.1033 and 92.1 / 16.6 / 15.1 / 27.4 s. Jev is cheaper and faster by one to three orders of magnitude; it is higher than Opus 5 in workflow mode only on customer service (76.0 vs 72.4) and lower on the other three (61.8 vs 78.4, 61.7 vs 66.2, 71.6 vs 75.2).
claims.implication: Cost/latency multiples here are best case against frontier LLMs on the vendor workflows.
